title: Millions May Be Getting the Wrong Cholesterol Test
hook: A new study finds that apoB — a blood test measuring harmful cholesterol particles directly — beats standard LDL testing at identifying who actually needs more intensive treatment.
key_points: ApoB is a blood test that measures harmful cholesterol particles, rather than the cholesterol they carry.
A new study found apoB testing outperforms standard LDL cholesterol testing at identifying who needs more intensive treatment.
Using apoB to guide treatment decisions could prevent more heart attacks and strokes.
The approach was also found to be cost-effective for the U.S. healthcare system.
content_html: Standard cholesterol tests report LDL — the "bad" cholesterol — as a single number, but that number doesn't distinguish between a few large particles and many small ones. A new study argues that distinction matters more than it gets credit for: apoB, a test that measures the harmful particles directly, was found to outperform standard LDL testing at identifying who actually needs more intensive treatment.
extra_html: As ScienceDaily reports, using apoB to guide those treatment decisions could prevent more heart attacks and strokes than relying on LDL alone — and the researchers found the approach would remain cost-effective for the U.S. healthcare system, not just more accurate in a research setting. ApoB testing isn't yet the default at most doctor's offices, but this is exactly the kind of evidence that shifts guidelines over time. If you're being monitored for heart-disease risk, it's a reasonable question to bring to your next checkup: is an apoB test worth adding to your bloodwork?
